extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing systematic review and meta-analysis protocols; journal editors, peer reviewers, funders, registries (e.g., PROSPERO), and educators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and reporting protocols for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (particularly those summarizing aggregate data/evaluations of interventions). The checklist defines required items a protocol should include to ensure transparency, reproducibility, and completeness of a priori methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1a Identify the report as a protocol of a systematic review
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the report as a protocol of a systematic review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label the document clearly as a protocol so readers and registries understand it presents an a priori plan rather than a completed review.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1b If the protocol is for an update of a previous systematic review, identify as such
rubrics_metrics.description: If the protocol is for an update of a previous systematic review, identify as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that the protocol updates an earlier review to clarify scope and relationship to prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2 Registration: If registered, provide the name of the registry and registration number
rubrics_metrics.description: If registered, provide the name of the registry (e.g., PROSPERO) and registration number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include registry name and identifier to facilitate linkage between protocol, registry entry, and later review.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3a Authors: Provide name, institutional affiliation, and e-mail address of all protocol authors; provide physical mailing address of corresponding author
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide name, institutional affiliation, and e-mail address of all protocol authors; provide physical mailing address of corresponding author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give complete contact details to enable accountability and queries; ensures transparency about who is responsible for the protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3b Contributions: Describe contributions of protocol authors and identify the guarantor of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe contributions of protocol authors and identify the guarantor of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State specific author roles (e.g., conception, methods, drafting) and who guarantees the integrity of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4 Amendments: If the protocol represents an amendment of a previously completed or published protocol, identify as such and list changes; otherwise, state plan for documenting important protocol amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: If the protocol represents an amendment of a previously completed or published protocol, identify as such and list changes; otherwise, state plan for documenting important protocol amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit any changes from prior protocols and describe how future amendments will be tracked and dated to preserve transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5a Sources: Indicate sources of financial or other support for the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate sources of financial or other support for the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare funding sources to allow readers to consider potential influences on the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5b Sponsor: Provide name for the review funder and/or sponsor
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide name for the review funder and/or sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List institutional funders/sponsors by name.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5c Role of sponsor/funder: Describe roles of funder(s), sponsor(s), and/or institution(s), if any, in developing the protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe roles of funder(s), sponsor(s), and/or institution(s), if any, in developing the protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify whether funders influenced design, conduct, analysis, or reporting; clarify independence where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6 Rationale: Describe the rationale for the review in the context of what is already known
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the rationale for the review in the context of what is already known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the review is needed and how it fits into existing evidence; situate objectives in current literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7 Objectives: Provide an explicit statement of the question(s) the review will address with reference to participants, interventions, comparators, and outcomes (PICO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an explicit statement of the question(s) the review will address with reference to participants, interventions, comparators, and outcomes (PICO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a structured PICO (or equivalent) formulation to define the review question(s) clearly and unambiguously.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8 Eligibility criteria: Specify the study characteristics (e.g., PICO, study design, setting, time frame) and report characteristics (e.g., years considered, language, publication status) to be used as criteria for eligibility for the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the study characteristics (e.g., PICO, study design, setting, time frame) and report characteristics (e.g., years considered, language, publication status) to be used as criteria for eligibility for the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define inclusion and exclusion criteria in sufficient detail to be reproducible and to allow readers to judge comprehensiveness and potential biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: 9 Information sources: Describe all intended information sources (e.g., electronic databases, contact with study authors, trial registers, or other grey literature sources) with planned dates of coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe all intended information sources (e.g., electronic databases, contact with study authors, trial registers, or other grey literature sources) with planned dates of coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List databases, registries, and other sources and specify the time span to be searched to allow replication and assessment of completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10 Search strategy: Present draft of search strategy to be used for at least one electronic database, including planned limits, such that it could be repeated
rubrics_metrics.description: Present draft of search strategy to be used for at least one electronic database, including planned limits, such that it could be repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a reproducible example search string (including limits) to demonstrate transparency and enable replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: 11a Data management: Describe the mechanism(s) that will be used to manage records and data throughout the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the mechanism(s) that will be used to manage records and data throughout the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain software, databases, deduplication, version control, and backup procedures to show how records and extracted data will be organized and preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: 11b Selection process: State the process that will be used for selecting studies (e.g., two independent reviewers) through each phase of the review (i.e., screening, eligibility, and inclusion in meta-analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: State the process that will be used for selecting studies (e.g., two independent reviewers) through each phase of the review (i.e., screening, eligibility, and inclusion in meta-analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe screening and eligibility procedures, number of reviewers, conflict resolution, and how reasons for exclusion will be recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: 11c Data collection process: Describe planned method of extracting data from reports (e.g., piloting forms, done independently, in duplicate), any processes for obtaining and confirming data from investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe planned method of extracting data from reports (e.g., piloting forms, done independently, in duplicate), any processes for obtaining and confirming data from investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify extraction forms, piloting, independent extraction, checking, and procedures for contacting authors for missing or unclear data.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12 Data items: List and define all variables for which data will be sought (e.g., PICO items, funding sources), any pre-planned data assumptions and simplifications
rubrics_metrics.description: List and define all variables for which data will be sought (e.g., PICO items, funding sources), any pre-planned data assumptions and simplifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify variables and any imputation/assumption rules to reduce post hoc decisions and selective reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: 13 Outcomes and prioritization: List and define all outcomes for which data will be sought, including prioritization of main and additional outcomes, with rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: List and define all outcomes for which data will be sought, including prioritization of main and additional outcomes, with rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly distinguish primary and secondary outcomes and justify prioritization to avoid outcome-selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: 14 Risk of bias in individual studies: Describe anticipated methods for assessing risk of bias of individual studies, including whether this will be done at the outcome or study level, or both; state how this information will be used in data synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe anticipated methods for assessing risk of bias of individual studies, including whether this will be done at the outcome or study level, or both; state how this information will be used in data synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify tools (e.g., Cochrane risk of bias), levels of assessment, and how bias assessments will affect inclusion, weighting, or sensitivity analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15a Criteria for quantitative synthesis: Describe criteria under which study data will be quantitatively synthesized
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe criteria under which study data will be quantitatively synthesized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State decision rules for when meta-analysis is appropriate (e.g., clinical and methodological homogeneity thresholds).

rubrics_metrics.name: 15b Planned summary measures and combining methods: If data are appropriate for quantitative synthesis, describe planned summary measures, methods of handling data, and methods of combining data from studies, including any planned exploration of consistency (e.g., I2, Kendall’s tau)
rubrics_metrics.description: If data are appropriate for quantitative synthesis, describe planned summary measures, methods of handling data, and methods of combining data from studies, including any planned exploration of consistency (e.g., I2, Kendall’s tau).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report effect measures (e.g., RR, OR, mean difference), handling of multi-arm trials, unit-of-analysis issues, and heterogeneity investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15c Proposed additional analyses: Describe any proposed additional analyses (e.g., sensitivity or subgroup analyses, meta-regression)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any proposed additional analyses (e.g., sensitivity or subgroup analyses, meta-regression).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify subgroup definitions, covariates for meta-regression, and sensitivity analyses to reduce data-driven findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15d If quantitative synthesis not appropriate, describe type of summary planned
rubrics_metrics.description: If quantitative synthesis is not appropriate, describe the type of summary planned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline planned narrative or qualitative synthesis approaches and strategies for summarizing and presenting findings without meta-analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: 16 Meta-bias(es): Specify any planned assessment of meta-bias(es) (e.g., publication bias across studies, selective reporting within studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify any planned assessment of meta-bias(es) (e.g., publication bias across studies, selective reporting within studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe methods for detecting publication bias (funnel plots, statistical tests) and for assessing selective outcome/reporting biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: 17 Confidence in cumulative evidence: Describe how the strength of the body of evidence will be assessed (e.g., GRADE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the strength of the body of evidence will be assessed (e.g., GRADE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the framework (e.g., GRADE) and criteria for judging overall confidence/quality of evidence and how this will be applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: Intended primary scope of PRISMA-P
rubrics_metrics.description: PRISMA-P is intended primarily for preparation of protocols of systematic reviews and meta-analyses that summarize aggregate data from studies, particularly evaluations of the effects of interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although developed for intervention reviews, reviewers preparing other types of review protocols are encouraged to use PRISMA-P where applicable; however PRISMA-P is not validated as a tool to judge methodological appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare protocol before PROSPERO registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should prepare a review protocol in advance of registering it in PROSPERO so that details requiring further consideration may be thought through in advance, avoiding the need for multiple amendments to registration information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completing a thorough protocol before registration reduces arbitrary changes and supports accurate registry entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use PRISMA-P to judge appropriateness of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not recommended to use the checklist as an assessment tool to gauge the appropriateness of the methods of a systematic review protocol; it has not been validated for that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRISMA-P is a reporting checklist (completeness/transparency), not a methodological quality appraisal instrument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to read Explanation & Elaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: It is strongly recommended that this checklist be read in conjunction with the PRISMA-P 2015 Explanation and Elaboration document for important clarification on the items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Explanation & Elaboration includes examples of good reporting, rationale, and evidence to help authors implement checklist items correctly.
